pr_title: kernel: fix race conditions with z_ready_thread
pr_body:
Several internal APIs wrote thread attributes (return value, mainly)
_after_ calling `z_ready_thread`. This is unsafe, at least in SMP,
because another core could have already picked up and run the thread.

Fixes #32800.

Signed-off-by: James Harris <james.harris@intel.com>

issue_context.title: Race conditions with setting thread attributes after `z_ready_thread`?
comments: @andyross - I'd be interested in your thoughts on this, as this is "gnarly scheduler stuff" :-)

Yes, once read_thread() returns the thread is in the queue and available to run at any time by this CPU or another.  The reschedule() call is just a cooperative point at which you can release a lock and allow a context switch.  And indeed, those spots in the IPC layer look wrong to me too.

(The posix layer using legacy irqlocks is something that should be fixed too, I think I might have mentioned that at one point)
Alright, that's what I thought; thanks for the doublecheck. I'll do up a PR to fix those cases then...

review_comments: Not really necessary, but done for consistency.
